subject: Model catalog attestation & pinning guidance for Globex RFI
messages:
From: Jane Carter <jane.carter@globex.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@globex.com
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFI: model provenance, licensing & pinning — initial questions

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking our RFI. Globex's procurement and security teams are consolidating vendor responses this quarter. We have three focused asks about your model catalog:

1) Can you provide a signed attestation that all models in the catalog were obtained under licenses that permit commercial redistribution and modification?
2) Describe your provenance tracking for each catalog entry (source repo, commit/tag, license text snapshot).
3) For customers that require pinned-model deployments, what is your pinning/rollback policy and how are pin updates communicated?

Can you reply with a short pack we can attach to our compliance binder (PDF or CSV preferred)? We need the pack by 2027-11-29 to keep our timeline.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Best,
Jane Carter
Senior Procurement Manager
Globex Corporation

---
Attachments: none
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Jane Carter <jane.carter@globex.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 23 Nov 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: model provenance, licensing & pinning — initial questions

Hi Jane — thanks for the clear asks. We're assembling a compliance pack and can deliver a signed attestation plus a catalog export that includes provenance metadata and license snapshots.

Quick notes:
- We will include an attestation PDF that covers model sourcing and license verification for cataloged models as of 2027-11-22.
- The catalog export will include: model id, canonical upstream source URL, source commit/tag, detected license text (snapshot), and recommended pin (semantic version/commit).
- For pinning: customers can pin to a cataloged model version. We support three update channels: stable (recommended for production), security-only (auto patch for critical CVEs), and experimental (rolling updates). Customers can request automatic notifications for update windows, or opt-in for manual applied updates.

We'd like to confirm one detail: does Globex require attestations that include cryptographic checksums of each model binary (SHA256), or is a license-text snapshot and source commit sufficient for your audit?

I'll attach an initial pack as soon as Marissa finalizes the attestation PDF and Karthik confirms the pinning wording.

Thanks — Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: none
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 24 Nov 2027 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: model provenance, licensing & pinning — initial questions

Kimberly / Karthik —

Drafts attached:
1) redwood_attestation_v1.pdf — signed attestation language that confirms our review process for cataloged models, the presence of license text snapshots, and the verification steps we run on upstream source artifacts. It includes a maintenance clause: attestations reflect catalog state as of the attestation date and are re-issued on major catalog syncs or at customer request.
2) model_catalog_export_20271122.csv — CSV export includes model_id, model_name, upstream_url, upstream_commit, license_detected, license_text_snapshot_link, sha256 (for artifacts we store), and suggested_pin.
3) pinning_policy_summary.docx — short internal wording summarizing pin channels and rollback mechanics.

Notes on SHA256: we currently compute checksums for artifacts we host in Redwood storage (hosted-models). For models where we index upstream references only (catalog-only entries) we provide the upstream commit/tag and license snapshot; we do not always host the artifact or compute a binary checksum unless the customer requests hosting or escrow.

If Globex requires an attestation that every catalog entry has an accompanying SHA256, we can scope that as a contract add-on (hosting/escrow + checksum generation).

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Security, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 25 Nov 2027 13:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: model provenance, licensing & pinning — initial questions

All — a couple of suggested edits to the pinning wording before we send externally:

- Clarify that 'pin' == a cataloged model version identifier (model_id + tag/commit) and that customer-managed pins are immutable on the customer's deployment until they authorize an update. We should avoid wording that implies Redwood will auto-change a customer's pinned version (except for the security-only channel where explicit opt-in is documented).
- Add rollback mechanics: when a customer requests rollback we must ensure the target version exists in the customer's allowed catalog and that any associated quantization/serialization artifacts are available for rollback path. This is a frequent legal ask.
- For provenance: add a short paragraph about license text snapshots being stored and timestamped with the attestation (to show historical claims).

I've edited pinning_policy_summary.docx and highlighted these changes. Approve if good and we send.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Catalog & Model Ops, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: RFI: model provenance, licensing & pinning — initial questions

Hi Jane — attached is the compliance pack for Globex: the signed attestation PDF, the catalog CSV export with provenance columns, and a short pinning policy summary. Highlights:

- Attestation: redwood_attestation_v1.pdf (signed by Product Security) confirms model license review and the process we use to snapshot license text and upstream commit metadata. Attestation is valid for the catalog state as of 2027-11-22.
- Provenance export: model_catalog_export_20271122.csv includes upstream URL, upstream commit/tag, license_detected, and a link to the stored license snapshot. For hosted artifacts we also include SHA256 checksums.
- Pinning policy: pinning_policy_summary.docx describes customer-controlled pins, three update channels (stable / security-only / experimental), rollback requirements, and notification options. Note: Redwood will not silently update a customer pinned deployment unless the customer has explicitly enabled the security-only auto-patch channel.

Next steps – please confirm whether you need SHA256 checksums for all catalog entries or only for hosted/escrowed models. If Globex requires full-binary checksums for every entry we can include that under an add-on (hosting + escrow + checksum generation).

Also included: DocuSign link if you want the attestation executed as an NDA/attestation addendum. Link: https://app.docusign.com/some-ds-link/ABC123

If you'd like a 20-minute walkthrough of the pack, I can schedule a slot this week; otherwise we'll assume this meets the binder requirements.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park

Received, and thanks for the quick turnaround. The pack looks good on first pass. Two follow-ups:
1) Globex security team prefers full SHA256 checksums where possible; for catalog-only entries not hosted by Redwood we will accept upstream commit + a signed attestation that the license text was snapshotted. Could you add a one-paragraph note in the attestation that confirms this hybrid approach is acceptable?
2) Can you confirm turnaround for a short walkthrough next Thurs (2027-12-02)? 30 minutes should suffice.

If you can update the attestation paragraph and share the DocuSign executed copy, we'll mark this as complete for our binder. Appreciate the flexibility.
